# Flat radius strictification removes compatibility for one shared canonical group

Let P be a finite set of distinct integer bases with |P|>=2 and

    conv(P) intersect Z^n=P.

Initially assume aff(P)=R^n. Let K be a centered full-dimensional
d-simplex of volume V, and let r_z>0 be compatible radii: the actual
hull of the fibers r_z K has exactly these integer fibers. Use the
one shared canonical cylindrical group

    H_i={l_i(x)>=0},    i=0,...,d,

where the barycentric coordinates of K are l_i+1/(d+1).
Every group cap has mixed mass Gamma_d M, where
M=V sum_z r_z^d, and the group covers the whole ambient space.

The flat strictification below works for d>=1. For d>=2 it implies:
in every neighborhood of this finite fiber family there is an actual
compatible simplex family with strictly greater mixed volume and
strictly smaller mass in EVERY one of these same fixed caps.
All cap planes, original cap budgets and integer bases are retained.

This concerns a selected single canonical group. Its budget need not
be the actual maximum-depth value. No arbitrary-cover or OC
classification is asserted.
The common-affine-centroid family is already OC-safe by the usual
weighted Doignon argument and ordinary Grunbaum: choose a weighted
integer base centerpoint, and every ambient cap through its fiber
centroid contains the centroids in one corresponding base halfspace.
Those fibers contribute at least their Gamma_d fractions. The new
result is removal of compatibility constraints for a selected-cover
physical variation, not a new OC case.

## 1. Exact normalization and strict Jensen gaps

Because 0 is interior to K, compatibility of the centered homothetic
fibers is equivalent to

    r_z >= sum_p alpha_p r_p

for every convex representation z=sum_p alpha_p p. Indeed the
corresponding Minkowski combination is (sum alpha_p r_p)K, and
containment in r_z K is exactly the scalar inequality.

Choose R>max_(z in P)||z||^2 and put

    phi(z)=R-||z||^2>0.

For epsilon>=0 define

    t_z=r_z+epsilon phi(z),
    lambda(epsilon)=[sum_z r_z^d / sum_z t_z^d]^(1/d),
    s_z=lambda(epsilon)t_z.                         (1)

All radii are positive. Their mixed volume and all shared canonical
cap masses are EXACTLY unchanged:

    V sum_z s_z^d=M,
    sum_z |s_z K intersect H_i|=Gamma_d M.           (2)

Moreover lambda tends to one and s_z tends to r_z as epsilon tends
to zero. For every representation of z,

    s_z-sum_p alpha_p s_p
       =lambda[(r_z-sum_p alpha_p r_p)
                   +epsilon sum_p alpha_p||p-z||^2].          (3)

Thus compatibility holds for every epsilon>=0, and is strict for
epsilon>0 whenever some positive coefficient belongs to p!=z.
This calculation uses strict concavity on the base coordinates;
no geometric equality classification is assumed.

## 2. A uniform margin after excluding the target

For a base z, consider convex representations of z using only
P without z. If none exists, z is a vertex of conv(P), and its
fiber imposes no interpolation constraint on the other fibers.
Otherwise all such representations satisfy, by (3),

    s_z-sum_(p!=z) alpha_p s_p
           >=lambda epsilon delta_P^2,
    delta_P^2=min_(p!=q in P)||p-q||^2>=1.           (4)

The bound holds on the entire compact representation polytope,
not merely its finitely many vertices. If a representation includes
z with weight less than one, normalize the remaining weights:
they again represent z, now without z. This removes the apparent
vanishing gap caused by representations with self-weight tending
to one.

Let

    Delta=min{lambda epsilon delta_P^2,
                         (1/2) min_z s_z}>0.         (5)

Then (4) holds with Delta at every nonvertex target. If every base
is a vertex, one may instead take Delta=(1/2)min_z s_z; there are
no excluded-target interpolation constraints at all.

## 3. An open neighborhood of independently variable actual fibers

Choose rho>0 with rho Ball contained in K. Fix epsilon>0, and
choose a common Hausdorff radius

    0<eta<rho Delta/4.                               (6)

Let L_z be ANY compact convex body with
d_H(L_z,s_z K)<eta, independently for all z. Hausdorff comparison
of support functions gives

    (s_z-eta/rho)K contained in L_z
        contained in s_z K+eta Ball.                (7)

For the lower inclusion, on unit directions h_(s_z K)-eta<=h_Lz,
while h_(s_z-eta/rho)K<=h_(s_z K)-eta because h_K>=rho
on those directions.
All displayed inner scale factors are positive by (5)-(6).

For a representation of z without z, (4) and the upper inclusion
give

    sum_(p!=z) alpha_p L_p
       contained in (sum alpha_p s_p)K+eta Ball
       contained in (s_z-Delta+eta/rho)K
       compactly contained in (s_z-eta/rho)K
       contained in L_z.                            (8)

The middle compact containment follows from
Delta-2eta/rho>0 and 0 in int K. Thus it is uniform over all
representations and all the independent choices of L_p.

Let C(L)=conv union_(z in P) ({z} times L_z).
Its projection is conv(P), so lattice completeness excludes every
other integer base. Any point of its fiber at z is a Minkowski
combination associated with a representation of z. If the weight
of its own source fiber is one, the point is already in L_z.
Otherwise normalize the other weights as in Section 2, apply
(8), and take a convex combination with the possible own-fiber
point. It still belongs to L_z. The reverse inclusion is built
into the hull. Hence

    C(L)_z=L_z for every z in P.                    (9)

Every L_z is full dimensional by (7). Since P affinely spans R^n,
the hull C(L) is a full-dimensional body in R^(n+d). This proves
an actual open neighborhood of independent fiber changes, not just
strict inequalities on a finite list of proposed directions.
In particular it permits all sufficiently small labeled physical
simplex vertex motions, their translations and their accelerations.

## 4. Two unequal free simplex volumes still give a positive shared-cap mode

Now assume d>=2 and put m=d+1, Gamma=(d/m)^d.
At the strictly compatible family s_z K, let V_z=s_z^d V.
Use barycentric physical vertex matrices W_z near I for each fiber.
The same fixed cylindrical cap has exact local volume

    F_zi(W_z)
       =V_z det W_z (W_zii-1/m)^d
                       /product_(j!=i)(W_zii-W_zij).           (10)

Its first derivative is Gamma V_z(T_z+R_zi), where T_z is
the trace and R_zi the row sum of the vertex velocity.
The objective-one shared stress is always

    ell_i=1/(m Gamma).

The canonical physical Hessian from
candidate ca3ec9792c38df0f is V_z Q on this fiber.
Its positive lift, parameterized by c with sum_i c_i=0, is

    A_ij=(m c_j+c_i)/(dm-1), i!=j,
    B_ii=-c_i,    B_ij=A_ij,

    T=0,    R=-dm c/(dm-1),
    Q(B)=q_d||c||^2,
    q_d=(d^2-1)/[d(dm-1)]>0.                        (11)

Choose any two distinct bases p,q and any nonzero such c.
Use the lift of c at p, and the lift of -(V_p/V_q)c at q.
All other fiber velocities are zero. Then every first shared cap
derivative vanishes, as does the total first volume derivative.
The aggregate Lagrangian second derivative is

    H=q_d||c||^2[V_p+V_p^2/V_q]>0.                 (12)

Thus equality of the two volumes is unnecessary.

## 5. Physical acceleration preserving every original budget

The full first derivative map of the m shared caps is onto, using
just fiber p. For a desired cap derivative vector f in volume units,
put

    T=(sum_i f_i)/(m Gamma V_p),
    R_i=f_i/(Gamma V_p)-T,
    A=(T/d)(I-11^T/m)+(1/m)R 1^T.                  (13)

It has zero column sums, trace T and row sums R. Equation (10)
shows that its m cap derivatives are exactly f.

Let q_i be the straight-path second derivatives of the global caps
along the two-fiber critical velocity in Section 4. Set

    e=Gamma H/2>0,

and choose a second acceleration on fiber p by (13), with
f_i=-e-q_i. The resulting polynomial physical path has

    C_i'(0)=M'(0)=0,
    C_i''(0)=-e for every i,
    M''(0)=H-e/Gamma=H/2>0.                        (14)

The last identity follows from objective-one stationarity and the
definition of H. All other fibers except p,q stay fixed. Exact
smoothness of (10) then gives, for all sufficiently small positive
times, strictly increased volume and strictly decreased mass in
every fixed canonical cap.

Section 3 supplies a genuine common open feasibility neighborhood
for these vertex motions and accelerations. Choosing the time small
keeps them there, as well as in the proper one-positive-vertex
cap chamber. Therefore no active compatibility relation from the
original family is being ignored.

## 6. Local escape from the original possibly non-strict family

The first stage (1) converges to the original finite fiber family
and preserves all of its cap budgets and its objective exactly.
For any prescribed neighborhood choose epsilon>0 sufficiently small
that this strictified family remains in that neighborhood. Then
choose a sufficiently short improving path from Sections 4-5.
It remains in the same neighborhood, has volume strictly larger
than the ORIGINAL M, and has every original shared cap mass
strictly below Gamma M.

The actual hull varies continuously with its finite compact fibers,
so the statement also holds in the Hausdorff topology of those
hulls. If one initially specified a larger convex body with the same
integer fibers, the conclusion is about its finite source data and
the hull realizing those data; no unsupported Hausdorff approximation
to unrelated real-base parts of that larger body is asserted.

Only one selected shared canonical group is preserved by the flat
stage. It is not claimed to preserve cap masses for another group
with different offsets or directions.

In d=1 this final escape is false: the two canonical opposite caps
partition every positive one-dimensional fiber up to null boundary.
Keeping their two budgets M/2 forces total mixed mass at most M.
The strictification and open-neighborhood conclusions of Sections
1-3 remain valid, but the positive Hessian in (11) requires d>=2.

## 7. Affine centroid fields and deficient base rank

If the reference fibers are c(z)+r_z K, with c(z)=Bz+c affine,
the allowed shear x->x-c(z) reduces them to the centered case.
Its fiber Jacobian is one and it leaves the integer base unchanged.
The shared caps in original coordinates are
l_i(x-c(z))>=0. Apply the construction after the shear and map it
back; all mixed masses, actual compatibility and fixed cap budgets
are preserved.

If aff(P) has dimension k<n, work in its saturated integer lattice.
Choose z_0 in P and let L=span_R(P-z_0).
The lattice L intersect Z^n is saturated and has rank k, so an
integer basis extends to a basis of Z^n. An integer translation
and unimodular change of base coordinates therefore identify
aff(P) with R^k times {0}, and preserve lattice completeness.
Apply the theorem in that relative base space. The resulting hull
is full dimensional there, of dimension k+d; its mixed d-volume
measure and all integer fibers are unchanged under the map back.
No completion to a full (n+d)-dimensional ambient body is required
or asserted by this relative version.
